notes: Directly continues IMG_5641. Fully transcribed (67 rows, 27 Apr 1937 - c. Apr 1938; CORRECTED per IMG_5643 - see that row). Calcutta, Vizagapatam, the recurring unresolved 'bey' code (8th occurrence), Aden/Suez/Gibraltar, London/Dover/Hull, Dunkirk, a new port (Middlesbrough) with an unexplained 6-week gap before its own sailing, Dunnet Head, Glasgow, Liverpool, a South Africa circuit that doesn't fully resolve chronologically (Table Bay/Port Elizabeth/East London entries out of order, plus a new unresolved code 'N.f.'), Mauritius, Lourenco Marques, Beira, Port Natal, Table Bay, a new port (Dakar), Liverpool, Manchester (Ship Canal), Glasgow, Liverpool, Gibraltar, Port Said/Suez, Calcutta again, Rangoon, Ceylon, Aden, and then the card's major event: **a serious grounding casualty, the ship going ashore off Perim** (entry circled by the clerk, corrected to 2 Apr 1938 - see below), with blue paragraph notes reading 'ashore off Perim', 'Position serious' and 're cargo discharge + jettison' - cargo had to be discharged and jettisoned to refloat her. This casualty coincides with an unusually dense run of captain changes in the card's footer (Walmsley, then Edge, Barclay and Evans all within about five weeks of early 1938), almost certainly related. A further run of blue parenthetical entries referencing Aden and Liverpool into early April, confirmed by IMG_5643 to be Lloyd's Agent casualty reports rather than real port calls. Card ends 'P.T.O.', continued on IMG_5643. New ports added to ports.csv: Middlesbrough, Dakar. DATE CORRECTION (made after transcribing IMG_5643): the grounding entry originally read as '22/2' is actually '2/4' (2 April) - IMG_5643 opens with an explicit, unambiguous cross-reference and a detailed dated salvage log that supersedes this card's own reading. The correction resolves what was flagged as this card's most significant chronological anomaly - with it, Calcutta/Rangoon/Ceylon/Aden now fall cleanly before the grounding instead of after.

captains: D.O. Evans (carried over from IMG_5642); G. Roberts (from 3 Oct 1938)
notes: Directly continues IMG_5642. Fully transcribed (54 rows, 2 Apr 1938 - Nov 1938). Opens with a detailed, dated blue salvage log for the Perim grounding introduced at the end of IMG_5642 (corrected there to 2 Apr 1938): a long run of Lloyd's Agent reports via London, marked '(Lo)' and dated almost daily through April, tracking the casualty from grounding through 'Refloated' (9 Apr), 'Damage serious' and 'Bottom very badly damaged' (mid-late Apr), to 'the repairs & jettison of cargo' (2 May) and finally 'Left Perim 28/5' - nearly two months aground/under repair. The voyage then resumes: Port Sudan, Suez, Port Said, two Mediterranean position reports (one an explicit lat/long, 'in abt 33N 25E', south of Crete; one 'off Cani Rocks' near Bizerte), Gibraltar, London, Dover, Avonmouth/Barry, Liverpool, Shields (with an unexplained ~2-month stay), London again, Gibraltar, Port Said/Suez, and then the ship's first appearance in the Persian Gulf: a new port (Jeddah), Aden, Bahrain, a new port (Bushire), a new port (Khor Musa Bar, the approach to Bandar Shahpur) - card ends mid-entry ('Bandar Sh...') with 'Continued on Card No. 7' (not yet identified). Captain changed mid-card (Evans to G. Roberts, 3 Oct 1938). New ports added to ports.csv: Jeddah, Bushire, Khor Musa Bar. One unresolved code, 'Bchy', between two London calls and Gibraltar.
